This is an unnecessary restriction. Karma as an incentive to submit content is a good thing, not a bad thing. A select group of people having more karma does not negatively impact anyone else's user experience. I do not feel hindered in any way by someone with 2x, 4x, or 10x more karma than I do. The existence of someone whose name appears more frequently than mine or is otherwise much more active, does not inhibit me from making my own submissions any way. If someone does not submit content, it is probably because they don't have any content to submit or are more interested in consumption of content. I believe the existence of a minority contributing the most is the pareto principle and/or the 1% rule at work.

1-10% of the population will always be more active than the rest. The same thing will happen with restrictions in place, but turnover of content will be much slower. That is, I would hypothesize that with restrictions in place, we'll still see the same people post more relative to those not posting, albeit now with a cap on their posting power. That's because a regime change (through restrictions on group A) does not motivate or give any more incentive for those in group B to post. This is like punishing someone who does more work to get those who don't put in much work to work more. It is a reactionary move in response to perceptions.

This problem of perception at the moment is due to low total size of users. As total user size grows, we should see the power user group grow with that. As the absolute numbers of the power users grow, the perception that a minority dominate discourse will go away (the phenomena will still exist, but it will not be that noticeable.) It only exists at the moment because the power user group consists of like 5-10 people at the moment so it's very noticeable but I think it will be less noticeable as diversity amongst this group grows.

The solution is to encourage those who are not posting much at the moment to post, not by restrictions and trying to control those who are contributing the most. It's also very inhibitory at this stage when growth is desired.
